Aisha (CS): Hey @Carlos — quick check: you mentioned Amber staging saw lots of 429s during SDK onboarding live-test earlier today? Can you drop the failing logs here so we can triage quickly?
Carlos (Customer): yes, we spun up 40 workers to warm clients and saw tons of 429s from /v1/preflight. Example response: 
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Retry-After: 3
{ "error": "rate_limited", "scope": "preflight" }
We've got short TTLs for tokens (30s) and do a refresh on each worker start.
Aisha (CS): thanks. Do you use the official JS SDK or rolling your own preflight?
Carlos (Customer): official JS SDK, v1.2.3, running in a serverless warmup job. We call `client.init()` from each worker on cold start.
Devon (SDK): pinging in — if every worker calls `init()` at once that's the common preflight storm. SDK has `initConcurrencyLimit` but it's opt-in. What's your current concurrency?
Carlos (Customer): it's 40 parallel. Noted `initConcurrencyLimit` — didn't know about that.
Ben (Eng): Also check if you have `ephemeralToken.refresh()` happening per worker. If you refresh at sub-minute TTLs you can create a thundering herd.
Carlos (Customer): we are renewing tokens proactively every 20s because TTL is 30s.
ryan_ops: deploy-bot: rollout 4098765400 -> amber-staging succeeded :rocket:
Aisha (CS): ok here's a short mitigation plan you can try now in staging: 
1) Reduce parallel init: set `initConcurrencyLimit: 4` in the SDK options.
2) Increase token TTL tolerance: treat token valid for TTL - 10s to avoid racing refreshes.
3) Add jitter/splay to warmup so starts are spread over 30s.
4) If you need immediate scale, use one shared init proxy process that returns client handles to workers.
Devon (SDK): example config: ```js
const client = new RedwoodSDK({
  initConcurrencyLimit: 4,
  tokenGrace: 10, // seconds to keep using token before refresh
  warmupSplay: 250 // ms random delay per start
});
```
Carlos (Customer): nice. Any quick server-side knobs on your end?
Ben (Eng): we can temporarily bump the preflight burst window for the Amber org by 2x for 15 minutes while you test (no SLA change). Ping me when you flip the config.
Carlos (Customer): please, that'd help. flipping now to test.
Devon (SDK): also worth switching from `refreshOnStart` to `lazyRefresh` if your workers can tolerate a tiny auth delay. That avoids parallel refresh at boot.
Carlos (Customer): ok changed to `lazyRefresh` + `initConcurrencyLimit: 4` + added 100-500ms splay. Re-running warmup now.
Aisha (CS): any errors yet?
Carlos (Customer): first run looks way better. A few 429s in the first 10s then steady. logs: 
[2026-03-23T15:02:11Z] worker-12 GET /v1/preflight 200 
[2026-03-23T15:02:12Z] worker-03 GET /v1/preflight 429 Retry-After:1
[2026-03-23T15:02:13Z] worker-03 retry -> 200
Devon (SDK): perfect — that pattern (one or two transient 429s then recovery) is expected when throttles briefly engage. Let us know if you still see sustained 429s.
Carlos (Customer): thanks all. Ben — please proceed with the temporary burst bump while we validate for ~30m.
Ben (Eng): done, Amber org preflight burst increased 2x for 30m. monitor: https://internal.redwood.ai/monitor/amber/preflight (ops-only)
ryan_ops: alert: preflight-rate-limit-threshold breached but stabilized after 3m, no action required.
Aisha (CS): awesome — I'll follow up in an hour for a short retro and capture this as an onboarding playbook step. Carlos, any feedback on the SDK docs that would have helped earlier?
Carlos (Customer): a short checklist would help: recommended `initConcurrencyLimit` default, token refresh guidance, and a warmup splay example. I nearly missed `initConcurrencyLimit` in the changelog.
Devon (SDK): noted — we'll add a concise "warmup best practices" section and call out serverless patterns. I'll open a docs PR.
Aisha (CS): thanks team, marking this thread resolved for now. :white_check_mark:
